title: CLAY CITY VILLAGE BOARD MEETS
full_story:
The Clay City Village Board met Tuesday evening and included a visit from Clay County Sheriff Andy Myers and taking action on a variance request for single mom seeking to make a fresh start.

Mayor Mike Delonshaw called the meeting to order and trustees quickly approved the past meeting minutes and the bills.  Clerk Shannon Hall stated that Clay City Civis is seeking to host an event at Mills Park and consensus seemed to be for approval, however there was no formal action taken.

Clay County Sheriff Andy Myers rose to his feet to inform the board that the Clay City School Board had voted to approve a contract with the sheriff’s office to provide an SRO (School Resource Officer) at the school.  It’s the first time that an agreement has been formalized and Myers sought to tell the board how it would affect the village.  He said that he now plans to hire another deputy this summer, however they will need to go through the academy and training and will start to make an impact in late Fall.  But he said his intention for them to play more of an active role in investigations.  He noted that the SAFE-T Act, enacted in 2021, continues to cause problems around the state in the eyes of law enforcement officials.  Myers stated the statute keeps them busier than ever and with limited bail, suspects are quickly released

And they often get into further trouble.  The sheriff said his goal is to provide adequate coverage and put anyone in a bind.

Next Kali Mainer addressed trustees to seek a variance to the village policy of not allowing older mobile homes into town.  Mainer said she is newly divorced and she and her three teenage kids want to stay in Clay City.  She stated that she has purchased a 1987 mobile home that has passed inspection and offered several photos of the home for trustees to inspect.  She adds that once it is in place she plans to paint it white with black shutters.  Mainer intends to put the home on a lot on Martha Lane.  When trustees questioned where it was and they were told, there was an unmistakable pause.  Sense this, Mainer said she knew the area was a mess right now, but she pledged to get it cleaned up this weekend.  She further stated her plans are to keep the area tidy and to eventually build on with the construction of a roof over the home.  She said she seeks to be a good neighbor and asked trustees to approve her variance request.  After answering a couple more questions, trustees unanimously approved her request.  Mainer became emotional with the approval and she and her family left the meeting with their thanks to the village board.  Once they were what they considered out of earshot, they could be heard celebrating their good fortune.  Trustee Beth Prosser, attending remotely, said with the clean up work they will be doing, she wondered aloud whether the village might offer her some assistance with a Rolloff unit which she believed would be needed and other trustees appeared supportive of the idea.

Brandon Bridges with Charleston Engineering from Olney presented the proposal for the annual MFT Oil and Chipping of village streets.  Bridges stated that the proposal presented by Larry Heuerman Trucking of Montrose came in $2,600 below the Engineer’s Estimate and recommend the board accept it.  After a couple of questions were answered, trustees unanimously approved the Heuerman bid of $39,457.  Sue Lindeman stated the village has learned that it’s application for the Safe Routes to School Grant has been approved and she thought everyone should know that.  The project will update sidewalks between Main St. and Clay City Schools to be ADA (Americans with Disabilities Act) compliant and increase the width to five feet.  While news of the grant awarding is now public, it will be several months or potentially over a year before construction begins.

Mayor Delonshaw noted Attorney Barry Bright’s absence and stated that Bright had informed him that his final day will be December 31, due to declining health.

Village Clerk Shannon Hall reported that Magoo and Associates of Effingham has lost their graphic designer and the village may need to find another company to work on its website.  Hall then reviewed the monthly cash balances and transfers report and noted a large discrepancy with water.  That caused Trustee Sue Lindeman to state that the figure was a pretty big discrepancy and told fellow members to be wary about next month too.  She asked about the water and sewer survey and was told the process takes 30-60 days to complete.  Hall said she would like to attend clerk training at the MCI Institute/Academy in Bloomington, October 4-9.  She said for past years she attended on a scholarship, and she will apply for it again and expects it to be awarded to her again.  Trustees approved her request to attend.

Before the meeting adjourned, Sue Lindeman requested to review closed session minutes, and Clerk Hall presented them to trustees.  With all business complete, the meeting adjourned.

title: CLAY COUNTY SHERIFF’S REPORT
full_story:
On Monday, the Clay County Sheriff’s Office served two search warrants in the Clay City Area relating to ongoing investigations.  During the course of the execution of these warrants, seven people were taken into custody, two were later released, and multiple stolen vehicles were recovered along with counterfeit money.

At approximately 12:03 pm, the sheriff’s office served a search warrant at a property on Tower Road in Clay City Township.  As a result of the search warrant, Jesse C. Harvel, 30, of Clay City, was arrested for the offenses of Possession of Stolen Property and Possession of Ammunition by a Felon.  Also arrested was Jade A. Fatheree, 25, of Clay City, on a Clay County Contempt Warrant (No Bond) on an original charge of Operating an Uninsured Motor Vehicle.  Both subjects were transported to the Clay County Jail.

At approximately 6:38 pm, the sheriff’s office served a search warrant at a property on Clark Avenue in Clay City.  As a result of the search warrant, Cody A. Turner, 37, of Clay City, Savahnnah C. Dulaney, 26, of Clay City, and Bradley W. Beaulieu, 61, of Olney, were arrested and transported to the Clay County Jail.  Turner was arrested for the offenses of Possession of Methamphetamine, Forgery and Possession of Unassigned Title(s), Dulaney and Beaulieu were both arrested for the offense of Possession of Methamphetamine.

The Sheriff’s Office was assisted by the Flora Police Department, Salem Police Department and Clay County State’s Attorney Phillip Givens.

The charge is merely an accusation, and the defendant is presumed innocent unless proven guilty.

title: ROTARY PICKLEBALL TOURNAMENT
full_story:
The Flora Rotary Club is sponsoring its 1st Annual Pickleball Tournament the weekend of June 19th and 20th at the Rotary Pickleball Courts.

On June 19th from 4:30 to 6:30 pm Senior’s age 55 and up will play and from 6:30 to 8:30 pm those 18 and under will play.  Then on Saturday from 8 to 10:00 am men’s doubles intermediates will play, from 10:00 to 12:00 am Men’s doubles advanced will play.  Women’s doubles intermediate will play from 12:00 to 2:00 pm, With women’s doubles advanced will play from 2:00 to 4 pm.  Mixed doubles intermediate will take the courts from 4 to 6 pm, and mixed doubles advanced will play from 6 to 8 pm.

Entry fee is $30 per person and sign up is available through a QR code on event flyers and more information is available on the Flora Rotary Facebook page.  Each team is guaranteed 5 games.  There is a maximum of 12 teams per division so sign up soon.  Registration deadline is June 12th.  Division winners will receive their entry fee back.

Joel Hackney from the Flora Rotary Club will be the guest today on the ReVue to talk about the Pickleball Tournament.  Because of todays North Clay Sectional Semifinal Baseball Game, the ReVue will be heard at 1 pm.

title: PLUMMER ICASH EVENTS
full_story:
State Senator Jason Plummer is hosting an ICASH event in partnership with the Illinois State Treasurer’s Office.  Constituents are encouraged to stop by to check if they are owed unclaimed property and receive assistance filing a claim.

State Senator Jason Plummer said, “Too often, folks don’t realize they may have money or property waiting to be claimed.  These ICASH events make it easy for residents to stop by, get help from professionals, and find out if they have unclaimed property.  My goal is to make this service more convenient and ensure people get the assistance they need to reclaim what’s rightfully theirs.  The Treasurer’s Office has over $5 billion in unclaimed property owed to Illinois residents.”

The ICASH event will be at the Flora Volunteer Fire Department on Tuesday, June 9th from 10 am to 2 pm.

ICASH events help residents across Illinois locate and reclaim unclaimed property.  Since 2015, more than $2.5 billion in assets have been returned to Illinoisans.  Unclaimed property can include everything from forgotten bank accounts and uncashed checks to insurance payments, stocks, and even the contents of safe deposit boxes.

No reservations are required.  For more information, call Senator Plummer’s office at 618-283-3000.

title: PLANNING MEETING
full_story:
The Illinois Housing Development Authority (IHDA) is launching a statewide planning initiative this year aimed at shaping future housing policy and investment decisions across Illinois.

This effort, called the Illinois Housing Blueprint, is designed to help municipalities, state agencies, nonprofit organizations and local leaders better understand how housing connects to regional economic development and community needs.  IHDA says the blueprint will serve as a planning tool to guide targeted, community‑specific housing strategies.

As part of the process, IHDA will host a series of listening sessions across the state.  In our region the meeting will be held on June 18th from 11 to 1 pm in Effingham, to gather public input from residents, housing stakeholders and local officials.  The meeting will be held at Koerner Distributor, at 1601 Pike Avenue.

Illinois residents are encouraged to register in advance for listening sessions at ilhousingblueprint.org/community-outreach.  According to IHDA, community participation is critical to ensuring the blueprint reflects the needs of residents across Illinois and represents both urban and rural perspectives.

IHDA is also collecting feedback through a statewide housing survey available in both English and Spanish.  The survey is open to all Illinois residents and asks participants about housing needs, challenges and community priorities.  The survey can be accessed at arcg.is/1qPjKP1.

title: HONDA RECALL
full_story:
Nearly 100-thousand vehicles are being recalled by Honda due to an issue with airbags.  That’s according to the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration.

The issue involves a defect that could lead to the unintentional deployment of airbags.  Most of the models affected are the Accord Hybrid, the Honda Acura TLX and other Accord vehicles.

Honda had received 228 warranty claims as of May 14th, the recall notice said.  The company also said it has no reports of injuries or deaths related to the issue in the US from February 4th, 2021, to October 30th, 2025.

title: HPIA DETECTION’S DECLINE
full_story:
Detection’s of highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI) in poultry decreased nationwide in April.

Last month, 62,000 birds were impacted by HPAI, which was down significantly from 11.4 million in February, according to USDA’s Animal and Plant Health Inspection Service.

Dr. Staci Slager, assistant state veterinarian with the Illinois Department of Agriculture (IDOA), said there have been only six cases of HPAI in the state so far this year.

Historically, HPAI cases rise during wild bird migration in the spring and again during fall migration.

To monitor HPAI detections and review biosecurity tips, visit the website aphis.usda.gov/h5n1-hpai

Lactating dairy cattle in the state are no longer required to have a negative avian influenza test to exhibit at county and state fairs.

title: AGRICULTURE IN THE BUDGET
full_story:
Described as a “significant win” for farmers, Illinois Farm Bureau-supported changes to the Farmland Assessment Law were included in the state’s $55.9 billion fiscal year 2027 budget.

The changes, if approved by Governor JB Pritzker, would extend the current property tax treatment for vegetative filter strips through December 31st, 2031, adjust the formula used to calculate farmland values and make minor technical updates.  Overall, the updates are meant to make the formula more consistent and predictable for both landowners and taxing bodies.

“Unfortunately, yet again, the Family Farm Preservation Act failed to make it into any final budget package this year, despite extensive efforts of Farm Bureau members, county Farm Bureaus, IFB leadership and governmental affairs staff,” said Chris Davis, Illinois Farm Bureau director of state legislation.  “We’ll take some time to reassess our efforts this year and we’ll move forward to continue the effort to try to get an estate tax reform in the state of Illinois.”

Meanwhile, IFB successfully opposed the Wetlands Protection Act from advancing, which sought to broadly define wetlands as any area exceeding one-tenth of an acre capable of supporting vegetation.  The organization also successfully halted legislation that would have allowed all broadband providers receiving state or federal grants to access road rights-of-way on private property simply by providing notice to the landowner.  Farm Bureau expects these issues to return next session.

The state’s appropriations bill, approved by the Illinois General Assembly June 1st, also includes no cuts to the Illinois Department of Agriculture, Fall Covers for Spring Savings cover crop program or agricultural education, Davis said.

Funding also remained level at $4.5 million for the Soil and Water Conservation Districts (SWCD).  The SWCDs advocated for $10 million for the districts, but this was ultimately not included in the budget.

Meanwhile, 4-H Extension will see a slight budget increase of $32,800, while the county fair rehabilitation budget will increase by $54,700.

The entire spending plan, which now heads to the governor’s desk for his signature, is slightly smaller than the nearly $56 billion budget he first proposed in February and includes $800 million to $900 million in new revenues.

“Every element of the budget for the upcoming fiscal year was thoroughly deliberated with the aim of achieving widespread affordability for all Illinoisans,” Pritzker said.  “I look forward to signing the FY 27 budget and delivering for Illinois’ working families in all stages of life.”

Lawmakers also passed legislation limiting students’ access to cell phones during class and a bill protecting minors from “addictive social media algorithms,” both of which Pritzker said he looks forward to signing.

Opponents of the spending plan, including state Senator Sally Turner, and state Representative Ryan Spain, who said “this year’s largest-in-history state budget” does not deliver the relief Illinois families need as they struggle with rising costs.

“Budgets reflect priorities, and despite a record price tag, this budget continues to grow spending while many Illinois families struggle with rising costs and an economy that continues to lag behind much of the nation,” Turner said in a statement.

Additionally, Illinois will pause the annual July 1st Motor Fuel Tax increase of $0.013 per gallon until January.  Also aimed at addressing affordability, sales tax on school supplies, clothing and computers will be suspended August 7th through 16th.

Capitol News Illinois shared the state also plans to allocate $143 million to the Illinois Department of Healthcare and Family Services for the Health Benefits for Immigrant Seniors program launched in 2020.  The program provides healthcare coverage for undocumented immigrants over 65, who would not be eligible for coverage under Medicaid.
